newsitem.title: UK: UK B/socs net new approvals s/a 3.651 bln in Nov.
newsitem.headline: UK B/socs net new approvals s/a 3.651 bln in Nov.

text.p: The UK Building Societies Association (BSA) released the following data on lending (seasonally adjusted unless otherwise stated):
MORTGAGE ADVANCES AND NEW APPROVALS TO LEND (in 1000s)
NOTES - approval = borrower accepts offer of advance; advance = actual loan, on average some 10 wks after commitment; advances tend to reflect new approvals made 2 or 3 mths ago.
BSA director-general Adrian Coles said that on a seasonally adjusted basis, all of the lending measures fell compared with the previous month.
"However, the underlying trend is still firmly upwards with advances and approvals significantly higher than in the same month last year," he said.

"The slight fall in lending in November is not a sign of a faltering recovery but rather that it is more stable and likely to be sustainable in the longer term. This is good news for the economy and the housing and mortgage markets."
The decline in net receipts was due to savers withdrawing funds for Christmas shopping.
"In spite of this, building societes performed well in comparison with National Savings, where net sales fell by 68 percent on the previous month," Coles said.
"Taking seasonal factors into account, building society net receipts increased by 18 percent compared with October to their highest level for over a year."
